---
title: "Preparing raw acquisitions"
---

Some *TOFWERK TOFexplorer* `.h5` files contain raw TOF detection events but no integrated ion maps. This is typically
the case if the raw acquisition has never been analyzed in *TOFexplorer*, which adds information about integrated
peak windows into the file. ToFScope can still read these "raw" files and prepare a new copy by integrating the peak
windows recorded in the file. The original acquisition remains unchanged.

## Prepare a copy

When you open a raw acquisition without ion maps, ToFScope shows a preparation preview before starting:

1. Review the [number of peak windows and frames](#preparation-scope) and the [required free space](#preparation-space). Preparation can take several minutes, and the final size depends on compression.
2. Check or change the [prepared filename](#preparation-filename) and review the displayed destination folder.
3. Select [**Prepare and open**](#preparation-start) to create and open the copy, or **Back to files** to return without preparing it. Progress and cancellation controls are shown while preparation is running.

```{=html}
<figure class="figure">
  <div class="explore-overview">
    <img src="../assets/tofscope-raw-preparation.png" alt="Raw acquisition preparation preview with the number of windows and frames, required space, prepared filename, destination, and Prepare and open button.">
    <span id="preparation-scope" class="explore-highlight" style="left:8%;top:20%;width:84%;height:16%" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span id="preparation-space" class="explore-highlight" style="left:8%;top:39%;width:84%;height:11%" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span id="preparation-filename" class="explore-highlight" style="left:8%;top:53%;width:83%;height:15%" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span id="preparation-start" class="explore-highlight" style="left:72%;top:79%;width:19%;height:9%" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  </div>
  <figcaption class="figure-caption">The preparation preview describes the work, space required, and destination before creating a copy.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

The prepared copy retains raw events and metadata. If the file lacks timing or channel metadata, the preview describes the
fallback assumptions; continue only if they are appropriate for the acquisition, because incorrect assumptions can produce
incorrect counts.

## Understand the limits

Only channels present in the raw peak table can be reconstructed automatically. Note: strict numerical equivalence with the
commercial software is not guaranteed.
